conceptual_core.subject: Declared workflow topology
conceptual_core.focal_question: How do ordered workflow handoffs, shared hooks, and guarded feedback loops shape the architecture?
conceptual_core.supported_decision: Where should an operator enter, follow, or revisit the declared workflow topology?
conceptual_core.topology_thesis: The declared architecture groups 4 workflows into 1 families. Forward edges carry typed handoffs through each ordered stack, while shared hooks couple workflows and dashed returns preserve review or refinement loops.

legend.label: Forward handoff
legend.meaning: One hook materializes the typed input consumed by the next hook.

legend.label: Shared hook
legend.meaning: The same skill participates in more than one workflow stack.

legend.label: Guarded return
legend.meaning: A critic, refiner, or guard can return findings to an earlier decision surface.

feedback_loops.return_semantics: Critique, refinement, or guard findings may return to earlier workflow criteria or hooks; the return is not another forward sequence step.

conceptual_core.complexity: Architecture complexity concentrates where a shared hook has high fanout or a feedback edge crosses an otherwise ordered stack.
conceptual_core.reading_strategy: Start with one family and follow its ordered handoffs. Then inspect shared hooks for cross-stack coupling and feedback returns for iteration or closure behavior.
conceptual_core.evidence_boundary: This model is extracted from coordination contracts. It describes declared architecture, not current execution, hook activation, success, or runtime cost.

graph.library_reason: Best fit for this repo because workflow interactions are graph-theoretic, semantically typed, moderately sized, and need node/edge hover/click inspection, compound hierarchy, and multiple graph views rather than only large-scale WebGL rendering.

layout_strategy.workflow_hierarchy: Preset hierarchy layout: families contain workflows, workflows contain ordered hook steps.
layout_strategy.workflow_drilldown: Preset per-stack drill-down layout: one workflow at a time with large ordered hook nodes and explicit sequence or feedback edges.
layout_strategy.node_click_drilldown: Click-first drill-down layout: start from a workflow index and open one stack's ordered hooks by clicking its workflow node.
layout_strategy.cross_stack_interactions: Force-directed Cytoscape cose layout with typed spring rest lengths and elasticities, stronger node repulsion, overlap avoidance, and lower gravity to preserve the previous organic style while reducing clumping.

edge_semantics.family_contains_workflow: A workflow family contains a workflow stack.
edge_semantics.workflow_entry: A workflow starts at its first hook.
edge_semantics.workflow_sequence: One ordered hook step feeds the next hook step in the same workflow.
edge_semantics.workflow_reflective_loop: A guarded review/refinement path can send findings back to earlier criteria or hooks.
edge_semantics.stack_uses_skill: A workflow stack invokes a skill hook.
edge_semantics.skill_handoff: One ordered hook hands its output to the next hook in the same stack.
edge_semantics.reflective_feedback: A review/refinement/guard loop can feed findings back into the workflow definition.
edge_semantics.reflective_external_reference: A dashed boundary edge marks a reflective relation whose concrete target is outside the active view.

family_contains_workflow.description: Hierarchy edge from workflow family to one contained workflow stack.

workflow_entry.description: Entry edge from a workflow stack to its first ordered hook.

workflow_sequence.description: Ordered in-stack handoff where one hook's result becomes the next hook's input surface.

workflow_reflective_loop.description: Guarded reflective edge that can revise criteria, hooks, or workflow structure.

stack_uses_skill.description: Invocation edge from a workflow stack to a reusable skill hook.

skill_handoff.description: Cross-skill edge showing the expected output type handed to the next hook.

reflective_feedback.description: Cross-stack feedback edge from review/refinement/guard conclusions to the workflow definition.

reflective_external_reference.description: Dashed boundary edge used when a reflective target exists but the concrete target node is outside the active view.

workflow_hierarchy.title: Workflow Sequence And Hierarchy
workflow_hierarchy.description: Shows family -> workflow -> ordered hook steps, with explicit entry, next-step, and reflective-loop edges.
